 PREFACE

Radhamadhab College, Silchar takes privilege in presenting before NAAC the
Supplementary Self-Study Report of the college, which epitomizes a vivid picture of
the college, envisaging the core values promulgated by NAAC and at the same time
keeping in mind the mission and vision of the college. The main SSR included the
activities of the College till December 2014 and therefore the supplementary SSR has
been prepared incorporating the activities of the college since December 2014 till
date. The format of the SSR or AQAR as provided by NAAC sometimes leaves no
room to incorporate the detailed activities undertaken by the institution. Hence, this
SSR has been prepared incorporating the academic as well as non-academic activities
of the college.

The year 1971 heralded the establishment of Radhamadhab College, Silchar, one of
the premier institutions of higher education in South Assam catering to the needs of
sub-urban and rural people of the area, with the noble aspiration of uplifting the moral
and educational standards of the pupils who are socially, economically and
educationally disadvantaged. The first institute from Southern Assam and among the
affiliated colleges under Assam University, to be accredited by National Assessment
and Accreditation Council (NAAC), the college has created a niche for itself and is in
the process of adding new feathers to its cap every academic year.

Taking into account the fact that the teaching faculty, students, library and
administration are important stakeholders of an institution, the Supplementary SSR
has been prepared with a view to highlighting all these components along with the
available infrastructural facilities.

I am indeed thankful to the IQAC and members of the college fraternity for their
wholehearted support and cooperation in the process of preparation of this
Supplementary SSR. My thanks are also due to the members of the Governing Body
for the encouragement and support provided by them.
                                               Dr. Pronoy Ranjan Deb

                Profile of the Department of Economics


The Department of Bengali came into existence since the very inception of Radhamadhab
College in the year 1971.

The courses offered by the department are:

      •    +2 level : Higher Secondary Courses (Affiliated to Assam Higher Secondary
           Education Council, Guwahati)
      •    B.A. Programme : Three Years Degree Program ( both pass & honours) which is
           affiliated to Assam University (A central University), Silchar.


VISION & MISSION

      •    The department offers excellent learning facilities to enable the students to know
           about Bengali literature, language and culture of our society.
      •    Our department gives utmost importance to build character and emotional ethics of
           the human beings.
      •    We also want to prepare the students to meet the social challenges, such as, cultural
           degradation, moral devaluation etc.
      •    In addition to the regular studies, we also want to teach our students about the Bengali
           traditional culture and oral literature.

       SWOC ANALYSIS OF THE DEPARTMENT


Strength

We have energetic, dedicated and well qualified teachers in the department. It is
worthy to mention that since last few years our students comparatively performing
better result in our College as well as in University level. Apart from the result, our
students are also involving themselves in different activities of the college and proving
their leadership with excellence.

Weakness

Shortage of teachers is the major problem in our department. Presently we have only
three permanent and two part-time teachers with whom we are not able to explore new
activities in our department.

Opportunities

Literature is the mirror of history, culture and society. So, our responsibility is not
only to teach the students in the class. At the same time, we are to involve ourselves
with the greater society in and around us. Keeping in view of this, we can open
different social and linguistical survey of Cachar District, Folk and Cultural Study
Centre, Folk based Museum, etc.

Challenges

 Presently our department is performing better result in Assam University and Board of
Higher Secondary Council. We are to go forward with the present positive result and
in future our motto is to be the best department in the college as well in the University.

teaching) to be held from the forth coming semester (Even Semester).

on the eve of SARODSAV.



CONCULSION

A tree is known by its fruits and the quality of fruits are depend on the soil, water,
light and environment. Though the students of our college comes from the rural areas
and poor previous examination result, the Department of Bengali shows its
exceptional performance since the inception in respect of examination result not only
in Radhamadhab College but also in University level in comparision to the other
colleges of this area. Still we are hoping to go ahead with determination to keep up the
examination result and other activities of the department.

Year of establishment: 1971
Vision and Mission of the Department
Education has always been considered as instrumental in bringing desired changes in the
society. So in the present context the importance of the subject “Education” has been
enhanced. The versatility of the subject is going to emerge as science, technology as well as
social science. In view of these facts the dynamic nature of the field of Education is stressed
so that the national goal is attained.

    General Objective
            a. To acquaint the students with understanding of the concept of education.
            b. To develop the skills of an analysis of the components and processes of
               education.
            c. To develop skills and for application of knowledge gained in real life.
            d. To develop a deeper perception of the subject.
            e.
    Specific Objective
            a. To inculcate among the students scientific outlook and ability to perceive the
               practical problems of education.
            b. To make the students familiar with the processes of change and development
               of educational principles and methods , in relation to changing needs of the
               society.
            c. To develop social efficiency and the sense of loyalty to the Nation.
            d. Need of the subject Education is felt for professional growth of teachers.

   2013-2014:
• The Dept of Education has taken an initiative to organize a seminar on “Enviornmental
   Education” on 27th September 2013 with an aim to develop an organized effort to teach
   about how natural environment function and particularly, how human beings can manage
   their behaviour and eco-systems in order to live sustainably among the students. As it is
   learning process, it can increase pupil’s knowledge and awareness about the environment
   and associated challenges. It will also develop the necessary skills and expertise to
   address the challenges and will foster attitudes, motivations and commitments to make
   responsible action. About 20 papers on different dimensions of enviornmental problems
   like enviornmental hazards, green house effect, impact of population on natural
   environment, deforestation ,garbage management ,different aspects of pollution etc. were
   read out and discussed by the students. During interaction session, students were very
   lively. The outcome of the seminar laid a great impact upon the students of the
   department as well as other students attending the seminar to be more conscious and
   responsible to the environment.
  •    Considering the values and role of herbs in our day to day life, Department of
   Education organized an awareness programme entitled “Role of medicinal plants in
   our life” on October 2013, to create awareness among the general students about the
   importance, values and uses of herbs in human life. Another aim of the programme was to
   collect and preserve some varieties of herbal medicinal plants found around our local
   surroundings and to establish a nursery of herbal medicinal plants as a demonstration plot
   in the college campus. In continuation with the awareness programme , students from the
   Department, and from other Departments collected some herbs and plants and

Teaching Methods adopted to improve student learning:
  • Print outs and hand outs are distributed to the students.
  • Daily 5-7 minutes are spent in classes revising what was discussed in the previous day
       and questions from students are encouraged in the classes.
   • To encourage the visit library, students are given topics relating to the syllabus on
       which they make projects, assignments by using materials from the library.
   • Special classes and extra time is devoted for slow learners and advanced learners.
   • Group study is encouraged.
   • Discussion method, seminars, team teaching methods, group discussion and practice
       teaching are integrated with the lecture method. Assignment and interactive sessions
       are also integrated with the conventional methods of teaching.

 SWOT ANALYSIS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION:
     Strength
     • The Deptt. is staffed with well qualified, experienced and dedicated faculty.
     • The faculty is actively involved in research and undertaken projects.
     • The Deptt. has well-equipped laboratory with a laboratory assistant.
     • The greatest strength of the Deptt. is the quality of the students admitted who
             show potential for growth.
        • Good relationship between the students and faculty members.
        • Teacher student ratio is favourable in all the classes except TDC 1st semester.
        • Inter-disciplinary programme, guest lecture and seminar are organized in the
             Deptt.
        • Committed and hard working students.
        • Regular guidance, motivation and support from the faculty.
        •    Faculty members of the department encourage the students in co-curricular
             activities by organizing extempore speech, debate, seminar, etc.
        •    The department takes pride in producing competent teachers in making. Some
             alumni of this department is serving as lecturers.

        Weakness
        •    Shortage of teaching faculty.
        •    Lack of proper and adequate infrastructure.
        •    Inadequate number of regular faculty members in sanctioned post.
        •    Lack of qualified technical and support staff in the laboratory.

         Opportunities
        •    Diploma in value education may be introduced to promote the development of
             environmental education
        •    Undertaking projects under UGC and other guiding agencies.
        •    Undertaking action research for solving problems in teaching-learning process.
        •    Opportunity to start PG/B.Ed. and M.Ed. Courses for the profession of teaching.
        •    There is ample scope and avenues for competitive examination, social work
             and teaching profession.
        •    The department has strong opportunity to run a Tribal Studies Centre as
             maximum number of students in the department are tribal.
        •    Students are given exposure to departmental seminars, group discussions for
             their all round personality development.

            Challenges
         •    To increase the teacher-student ratio for efficient delivery of the curriculum.
         •    To cope with the changing teaching methodologies to suit classes with large
              number of students.
         •    Lack of placement opportunities for degree holders.
         •    To popularize the discipline and its applications in various fields of day to day
              life.
                                                                                           164
            •   To develop career-oriented mind sets in students.
           •   To encourage the students to participate in extension education and other co-
               curricular activities in inter and intra college.
           •   The department is well geared to face the challenging times. The subject
               education itself is a multi-disciplinary subject consisting of philosophy,
               psychology and sociology. It is indeed a challenge to imbibe in the students the
               qualities required to survive in this world. Philosophy gives us an ideal to
               follow, psychology shows us the ways and means and sociology provides us a
               ground for implementation of the above.

      Future Plan

       •   To undertake a project by the Honours students on socio-graphy
       •   To conduct a field-trip.

 SWOC ANALYSIS OF THE DEPARTMENT AND FUTURE PLANS

Strength
       1. The department is notably exceptional with experienced, co-operative, sincere and
          committed team of faculty.
       2. The college is equipped with a Language Lab. which is indeed an added
          advantage for the second language learners.
       3. The department is running a UGC sponsored Certificate Course in Functional
          English which has benefitted the learners a lot.
       4. The progress of students is monitored through unit tests, seminars, group
          discussions, recitation and debates.
       5. The teachers use ICT in honours class.
       6. Extension lectures by experts are organized and students from various colleges are
          invited for interaction.
       7. There is a resourceful departmental library.
       8. The Teachers try their best to cover and complete the syllabus in time as per the
          lesson plan and course distribution.
       9. We are highly privileged and remain grateful to the supporting non-teaching staff
          of the college for their sincere co-operation.

Weakness
     1. Poor student-teacher ratio in pass classes, consisting of approximately 250
         students. It becomes impossible to give individual drill and provide ample scope
         for application of newly learnt skill.
     2. The transition from annual to semester system left little time for extra curricular
         activities.
     3. Time constraint and shortage of teachers gives little scope for the teachers to
         attend conferences, workshops and other research oriented programmed.
     4. Learners have very weak base in English as it their 2nd language. Most of them are
         from vernacular schools and there is a tendency amongst the students to fall back
         into vernacularism.

       Opportunities
       1. We feel highly privileged to get the opportunity to polish and teach students with
          vernacular background.
       2. Extensive use of ICT for the benefits of the students.
       3. To Organise more inter-departmental seminars and guest lectures.

       Challenges
       1. The students are 1st generation learners, weak in English and pose a challenge for
          the teachers of the department especially in a class consisting of approximately
          250 students.
       2. To inspire and prepare the students to pursue their Higher Education in English
          literature and orient them about the prospects of mastering the global language.
       3. Helping the learners to overcome the psychological barriers and use the language
          unconsciously.

          PROFILE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HISTORY

The Department of History came into existence since the very inception of Radhamadhab
College in the year 1971. The courses offered by the department are:
   a. +2 level: Higher Secondary Courses (Affiliated to Assam Higher Secondary
       Education Council, Guwahati).
   b. B.A. Programme: Three Years Degree programme (pass & honours) which is
       affiliated to Assam University, Silchar (A Central University).


Vision & Mission:

   1. The department offers excellent learning facilities to enable the students to meet the
       challenges of future world & focuses on their all round development.
   2. To give utmost importance to the socially, economically marginalized sections of
       students

   3. To preserve and enrich the already rich socio-cultural traditions of the hinterland

   4. To prepare a student such that, when leaving college after completion of the three-
       year degree course, he/she is equipped with a positive frame of mind, has basic
       communication skills, should have acquired the ability to explain something logically,
       and above all, should have developed a balanced personality.

DEPARTMENTAL ACTIVITIES SESSION WISE:
2010-2011 :

  2010-11 witnessed the introduction of the semester system at UG level by the affiliating
university (Assam University, Silchar). The faculty members were involved in acquainting
the students about the new pattern of study. Introduction of new syllabus also necessitated the
task of managing study materials for the students.

2011-2012:
   Apart from imparting routine classes, the faculty members were involved in acquiring
  books for the college library after consulting catalogues of various publishers in order to
  cope up with the new syllabus introduced in the previous academic year. The students
  were taken to the central library and were shown the new books procured. A field trip was
  undertaken by the Department in 2012 to Kashpur (a historical site in this valley) which
  was sponsored by UGC. The students were given a practical insight of the archeological
  process and architectural patterns of which earlier they had only theoretical know-how.

2012-2013:
   In this session the faculty members introduced the system of ICT as per availability in
classroom teaching. Power point presentation of the various topics made the lessons lively.
The students became more attracted towards the subject because we were able to show
pictures of various events and personalities of whom they had only heard. A renewed interest
towards History as a subject was noticed among the students.
                                                                                            183
 2013-2014 :
   In the session, Honours students were given assignments and projects. For pass course
   students the faculty organised oral test and snap test regularly. In this session, three guest
   lecturers were organized for TDC first semester students. Dr. Dhrubhojyoti Dey,
   Assistant Professor of History, Guru Charan College, Silchar was invited to deliver guest
   lectures which incorporated the topics from the syllabus.

2014-2015:
   In this academic year, the affiliating university restructured the units of the syllabus and
    hence there arose the necessity of acquainting the students with the new pattern. Oral
    quiz was conducted in the class so that the students could tackle the objective type
    questions asked in the final examination. Guest lecture was organised wherein teachers
    from other departments of the college delivered lectures based on the syllabus as per
    their specialization.

2015-2016:
     A Quiz Competition was organized by the Deptt. in collaboration with Education &
  Philosophy Deptt. on 17th September, 2015. The programme was conducted by Sri
  Sudarshan Gupta, Assistant Professor of Deptt. of History. Ten teams participated in the
  competition. In this session, the department also organized guest lectures. Dr. Moynul
  Haque, Associate Professor and Head, History, Guru Charan College, Silchar delivered his

 SWOT ANALYSIS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HISTORY:
 Strength

   •   Sincerity of the faculty members. The faculty members provide study materials to
       the students in both hard and soft form.

   •   There exists a good coordination between the teachers of the department. The HOD
       extends all sorts of cooperation.

   •   Well-qualified teaching faculty (50% with Ph.D.) that caters to the need of the
       students and also publishes research papers.

   •   Provides peaceful and congenial atmosphere for teaching-learning process, which
       includes state-of-art library, ICT enabled classroom, technically equipped faculty
       etc.

 Weaknesses

   •   The students mostly come from the rural areas with a very mediocre base and
       therefore they often fail to cope up with the challenges of higher education in the
       form of syllabus and curriculum.

   •   Weak alumni consciousness.

   •   Weak consultancy output.

   •   Yet to offer CBCS pattern of education to the students by the affiliating University,
       which would help the students to score good marks.

   •   Defective syllabus: The syllabus is so vast in comparison with other subjects at the
       same level that students become afraid and are disinterested to study the subject.

 Opportunities

   •   Trend of increased enrolment in the subject.

       History as a subject is lucrative for appearing in competitive examination including
       Civil Services. Any sort of written interviews for job in any post do have some
       questions on History. This aspect is being gradually realized by the students.
                                                                                         187
   Threats

     •       Limited job opportunities after passing out traditional undergraduate courses.
     •       Large-scale exodus of bright students towards professional course.
     •       Mushrooming growth of private colleges.


The department has identified the following Future Plan of Action in order to upgrade the
department of History.

  Future Plan

     i)         To undertake quality research studies, consultancy and learning programmes
                and to collaborate with other stakeholders of higher education for quality
                evaluation, promotion and sustenance.
     ii)        To come up with departmental research journal (web version) for the upliftment
                of research culture.
     iii)       To organize National and International Seminars, Workshops, orientation
                programmes
     iv)        To initiate PG Department in the college campus.
     vi)        Department is also taking interest to invite expert teachers of History from
                various universities and Institute to orient the students and explore their interest
                of studying history.
     viii)      Department also has a plan to organize Guest lecture on syllabus based topic to
                inspire the students and develop their knowledge of the subject.
     ix)        Department to organise tour programmes in places of historical importance to
                make the past alive before the students.

Teaching Methods adopted to improve student learning:

   • The faculty provides the students with study materials.
   • Usually before beginning a new class a few moments is devoted revising what was
          discussed in the previous day
   • Questions from students are encouraged in the classes.
   • Special classes and extra endeavour is taken for slow learners and advanced learners.
   • The chalk and talk method is supplemented with ICT in order to make the lessons
          more lively. Assignment and interactive sessions are also integrated with the
          conventional methods of teaching.

        PROFILE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF PHILOSOPHY

1. Objectives of the Department: The study of Philosophy is integral to the cultivation of
   traits necessary for intellectual, moral, spiritual and social leadership. The objective of the
   Department is to produce liberally educated persons who possess basic cultural literacy,
   who are capable of articulate and logical reflection on the fundamental problems of
   human existence and who can take their place as responsible citizens in public affairs.

2. Motives of the Department: The Department in its endeavour to fulfill objectives
   undertakes key activities like moral and spiritual training to enhance intellectual and
   moral traits of students, publish Wall Magazine to bring out latent creativity of students.
   The Department since its inception in 1971 has been toiling hard to make the students
   intellectually, morally and spiritually sound individuals so that they can shoulder their
   social responsibility. To accomplish this task talks, guest lectures, departmental seminars,
   assignment writing etc. are organized. The Department also regularly takes H.S.1st Year
   and 2nd Year classes as because it is also one of the important parts our activities.

Besides these academic courses prescribed by the university the Department encourages
inter-disciplinary activities with an object of enabling students to think critically and to
enhance their analytical power. Other than this academic routine work, the faculty members
are actively engaged in writing book, publishing article and attending workshops, national
and international seminars etc.

11. SWOT analysis of the Department:
Strength: Faculty members are sincere, hard-working and maintain personal contact with
students as far as possible. Department also provides study materials to weak and
disadvantageous students.

Weakness:

The students mostly come from vernacular medium with a very poor and average base and
therefore, fail to cope up with medium of instruction (English) and challenges of higher
education in the form of syllabus and curriculum.

Insufficient faculty leading to the increase of Teacher-Student ratio.

Lack of uniform syllabus with all India level deters the students to compete at All India level.

Opportunities:

Given the proper infrastructural support and desired faculty the department can impart
training to students opting for civil services examination.

Threats:

Limited job opportunities after passing out traditional under graduate courses. With the
growing demand of employment opportunities among the students the syllabus need to be
restructured to make the subject more job-oriented, otherwise the number of students may
gradually decline.



Future Plan:

To observe World Philosophy day.

To arrange one or two special lecture on relevant issues.

To publish Departmental Research Journal.

SWOC analysis of the department

Strength
   • The department is 4 teachers department.
   • The teachers are belonging to different field of specialization such as Public
       Administration, Political Sociology, and International Organisation etc.
   • The department has both Pass and Honours course.
   • Due to 4 teachers department, the department can manage both pass and honours
       course without any difficulty.
   • Teacher-student relationship is cordial in the department.

Weakness
  • Teacher-student ratio is 50:1 for which teachers cannot take proper care personally.
                                                                                           206
    • There is lack of I.T. facility in the department.

Opportunity
  • Due to sufficiency of teachers the department can manage classes properly if one
     teacher is on leave.
  • Due to sufficiency of students area of competition among the students is wide for
     which talent among the students develops.
  • Due to 4 teachers department the teachers can interchange views if any discussion on
     academic problem arises.
  • Due to sufficiency of students, departmental seminars, interaction session, group
     discussions can be arranged in the department conveniently.
  • Due to Departmental Cabin teachers can devote properly in the preparation of the
     classroom lectures and also for constructive thinking for social issues.

Challenges
  • The department has the challenge to improve results of the department in both pass
      course and honours course.
  • The department has the challenge to develop the spirit of competition among the
      students for doing good result.
  • The department has the challenge to guide the student not only in academic field but
      also to build their career.

Future Plans

   • Political Science Department will undertake the following plans:-
   • To publish Departmental Wall-Magazine “The Vanguard” annually.
   • To publish a departmental journal provided financial grant is extended by
     the college authority.
   • To organize guest lecture on any burning topic of the nation or in the
     international scenario.
   • To organize departmental seminars in every semester.
   • To organize departmental debate in the department on any current issue of
     the nation.
   • To apply to U.G.C. or I.C.S.S.R. for funding a National Seminar.

establishment there was a single department i.e., Arts department functioning in the college.
After a long journey with a single Department (Arts) and because of increasing demand of
Commerce as a discipline and also the necessity of the locality and nearby, the authority have
decided to start Department of Commerce and as a result Department of Commerce started
functioning in the year 2007.

                             Academic Monitoring Cell

Teaching is an art. Presentation of materials is the style of the art. Producing quality in
teaching is the essence of the art. Teaching means helping students learn well by producing
good quality of materials. Teaching is one major aspects of academic life of the college and it
is the input from the personal scholarship that gives teaching its special flavour. Teaching's
major components are content, communication and feedback. There is a close relationship
between teaching and learning and it is possible to modify, improve and develop teaching
quality by adopting various innovative methods.
Academic development does not remain confined to teaching & learning activities only. It
encompasses all the activities both of internal and external environment as well. Quality
improvement in academic life needs continuous assessment of activities, review, re-design
and reform of all norms and activities required thereof to ensure further improvement. With
these purposes in view, the college has introduced a "mechanism" to obtain improvement in
                                                                                           227
 teaching learning experiences and to ensure quality in academic life of the college by
initiating "Academic Monitoring Cell" with the purpose of accomplishing the ultimate goal to
the college.

                           INTERNAL EVALUATION CELL



INTRODUCTION

Evaluation is an integral part of the academic process. Necessarily Internal Evaluation Cell
started its functioning since the college was established in the year 1971. At the beginning the
evaluation process of the college was done by some selective teachers engaged by the
Principal from time to time. The constituted body of the cell was formed under the name and
style “Internal Evaluation Cell” in the year 2004 for the first time. Since then the examination
process of the students is being monitored by the Internal Evaluation Cell.

MISSION & VISION

   1. Regular evaluation of the students through Unit Tests and other test like viva test,
      snap test, class test etc.
   2. To conduct the tests and to publish result in time.
   3. To detect the weak students by preparing the defaulter list after each unit test.
   4. To take necessary measure for weak students through remedial classes.
   5. To aware the concerned parents about the poor performance of the students.
   6. To issue Report Card to all students, though considering the various aspects, the same
      will be issued in phase manner.
   7. To detain the defaulter students in respect of very poor performance of result and
      class attendance from appearing in the final examination. The students are sometimes
      allowed to appear in the examination after taking an undertaking.
   8. Our vision is not to detain the students from appearing in the final examination, but to
      alert the concerned parents and students, so that they can attain better result in the
      final examination.


ACTIVITIES OF THE CELL

   1. To hold Unit Test for both H. S. and Degree students.

   2. To hold H. S First Year Final Examination as per guidelines of the Assam Higher
      Secondary Education Council.
   3. To take necessary measure to declare Unit Test and H. S. First Year Final
      Examination result.
   4. To take necessary measure for printing of question papers.

                                                                                            244
   5. To prepare invigilation duty chart for the smooth functioning of the examination.
  6. To decide what amount of centre fees will be collected from the students for H.S.
     First Year Final examination.
  7. To prepare the promotion guidelines of the students.

  1. The time schedule for H.S. Unit Test will be 90 minutes and TDC Semester Unit Test
     will be of 60 minutes duration. (See resolution no 2 of the meeting held on
     22.08.2012).
  2. The mark allocation for H. S. will be of 50 marks and TDC semester examination
     will be of 25 marks in each paper. (See resolution no 1 of the meeting held on
     22.08.2012). The marks allocation for each paper was maintained in every year.
     However, meeting of the cell is convened before each examination every year.
  3. The committee decided to incorporate the unit test routine in the college prospectus,

                       Discipline and Anti-Ragging Committee
Introduction: The primary objective of Discipline and Anti-Ragging Committee is to
maintain discipline and prevent ragging inside the classroom and within the campus. The
committee frames the code of conduct for students with a view to foster and to protect the
missions of the college, to foster moral and civic development of students in a safe and secure
learning environment. The Discipline Committee tries to inculcate higher values of honesty,
integrity, responsibility, mutual respect, fellow-feeling. The committee aims to educate
students to be responsible, civic minded citizens. To accomplish this task the committee
organizes orientation programme to acquaint the students with code of conduct framed by the
college, arranges guest lecture on value education etc.

The main concern of the committee is to maintain strict discipline and prevent ragging in any
form in and out of the classroom. The committee enforces strict dress code, prohibits the
usage of Cell Phone by the students inside the campus. The committee also ensures that all
the students attend classes without bunking. The code of conduct framed by the committee is
published in the prospectus and uploaded in the College website. The committee also takes an
undertaking from students at the time of admission jointly signed by the ward and parents.

At the beginning of every academic session students are being oriented by teachers in their
class about the rules and regulations of the college. In addition to this some other
programmes are also organized to develop moral and civic sense of students. In the academic
session 2013-14, the students were mainly counseled on the bad effects of ragging and
advised them not to indulge in any kind of ragging because that would invite severe
punishment. Students were also encouraged to take part in Youth Convention held at
Ramakrishna Mission, Silchar on “Nation Building and Vivekananda”. Some instruction
boards displaying the rules and regulations were hung in different corners of the college.

In 2014-15 session other than the routine work of orienting the students about the Do’s and
Don’ts, a three day workshop on “Youth and Stress Management” was held in collaboration
with Art of Living, Silchar Unit. A guest lecture on “Value Education” by Swami
Vaikuntanandaji of Silchar Ramakrishna Mission was also organized.

In 2015-16 a three orientation programme “On the introduction of new syllabus by the
university and new marking system” was held. Members of the committee and the IQAC
coordinator spoke on the occasion. A group of students were sent to take part in the Youth
Conference at Silchar Ramakrishna Mission on “Personality Development”

OBJECTIVES:

         Radhamadhab College Employees’ Medical Relief Fund was established in
01/09/1999. The aims & objective of the fund is to extend financial relief of an emergent
nature to the members of the fund in the event of Medical treatment. The relief may be

                    Research and Programme of Studies Cell

Guidelines and Functions:

The Research and Programme of Studies Cell promotes self-financing courses and it is a
functional unit under IQAC, Radhamadhab College. The Cell initiates from its beginning to
motivate the learners inside and outside the college campus to join additional courses like
Computer Learning, Mobile Repairing, Interior Designing or Library and Information
Science to acquire the scope and opportunity to become self employed and to become self-
sufficient in their future course of life. The Cell takes proper measures to enroll students
through proper admission process, counseling, and motivating to equip themselves so that
they can appropriately suit themselves with the ever changing scenario of modern generation
of knowledge. Since its inception, the Cell has ventured forth various programmes and
introduced different certificate and short term courses according to the need and number of
students available in the institution. The cell also has many other visions to fulfill in near
future for the upliftment and benefit of students.


Objectives
The primary objectives of the cell should be promote research culture for the improvement of
quality in education in the College, to encourage faculty members, learners to undertake
research, project work on various problems of the community, region and the country, and to
help the government and other agencies to solve the problems through research, to establish
linkage/ collaboration with state/ national/ international organizations for research and
training to help the college to generate revenue through consultation / expertise through
respective field of specialization and study to organize state level national level and
international level seminars and organizing fund from UGC or any other funding agencies
etc.

                                            SC/ST Cell


   1. INTRODUCTION
The government of India and the University Grant commission have given priority for
the development of SC/ST or weaker communities that are suffering from economic, social
and educational deprivations. The Constitution recognizes the SCs and STs as the two most
backward groups needing special care and protection. Moreover, democracy demands the
necessity to safeguard and foster the interests and necessities of the minority groups. The
University Grants Commission during the Eleventh and Twelfth Plan periodprovided
financial assistance for conducting special classes (remedial coaching) outside the regular
timetable to enable students belonging to SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer)/ Minority
communities, who need remedial coaching to come up to the level necessary for pursuing
higher studies efficiently and to reduce their failure and drop-out rate. Students belonging to
Other Backward Classes and General Candidates may also be allowed the benefit of such
coaching classes. A nominal fee (not exceeding the monthly tuition fee) may be charged from
the general candidates. However, physically challenged students and students who are
General Candidates coming from families with income below the poverty line (as guided by
the State/ UT/ Central Government) will be exempted from paying the fee.


   2. OBJECTIVES OF THE SCHEME

The Remedial Coaching is to be organized at Undergraduate and/or Postgraduate level with a
view to:
   i.  Improve the academic skills and linguistic proficiency of the students in various
       subjects.
  ii.  To raise their level of comprehension of basic subjects to provide a stronger
       foundation for further academic work.
 iii. To strengthen their knowledge skills and attitudes in such subjects where
       quantitative and qualitative techniques and laboratory activities are involved, so
       that the necessary guidance and training provided under the programme may
       enable the student to come up to the level necessary for pursuing higher
       studies efficiently.


   3. SC/ST CELL AT A GLANCE

The SC/ST Cell at Radhamadha College, Silchar was constituted in the year 2009. Since
then, the cell of the college has been functioning to promote higher education among
                                                                                           268
 underprivileged and weaker students, particularly belonging to the SC/ST/OBC(non-creamy
layer)/Minority communities by organising remedial coaching classes to enable them to
come up to the level necessary for pursuing higher studies efficiently. The main aim of
the Cell is to monitor the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Human Resource Development
(MHRD) and the University Grants Commission concerning higher education of the students
in the reserved category from time to time.

      STUDENTS’ WELFARE AND AMENITIES COMMITTEE

Academic Session 2010-11 to 2015-16:

The Students’ Welfare and Amenities Committee of Radhamadhab College is always taking
sincere efforts for all-round development of the students.
The committee initiates different schemes for the students which include participation at
various levels like cultural activities, debates, extension activities, self financing courses and
workshop etc to inculcate the spirit of self-reliance and boost the confidence among the
students. This committee also regularly reviews the conditions that contribute academic
success, personal development and well being of students including available form of
financial success. The committee also explores various funding agencies like public and
private undertakings, NGO’s or grants received from any organization or individuals to
enrich the fund of the committee so that committee is able to give more financial help to the
students. The committee also encourages the students to enrol for self-financing courses
either from college or from outside the college. Besides this, the committee provides financial
assistance in every academic session to the poor students on the basis of the collection of
fees. To inspire the students in general, the Committee also extends its cooperation to
motivate the students to participate in sports activities, publish article in the college journal
“Patraput” (a students’ magazine) and participate in cultural programmes. For regular health
check-up the committee always motivates the students to check-up their health from the
students Health Care Centre of the college.

Cachar district on 22.03.2015 (Sunday). A team of doctors attended the patients who were
later given free medicines. The said camp was organized in collaboration with Student’s
Health Care Centre of Radhamadhab College, Silchar. The team of doctors comprised of Dr.
Nijamuddin Khan, Dr. Kapan Debnath, Dr. Ramprasad Powey, Dr. Rudra Prakash, Dr.
Sanchita Kalita and Jerina Nazrina of Silchar Medical College and Hospital.

Sudarshan Gupta, a few teaching staff and the NSS volunteers of the college were present at
the medical camp. Two pharmacists, Satyajit Dutta Choudhury and Arunabha Debroy
extended their help in distributing medicines to the patients. The NSS volunteers played a
significant role in this event. They worked in several groups. They enlisted the names of the
patients who came for check up, helped to form queue, and assisted the doctors and
pharmacists in distribution of medicine. It was indeed a unique experience where the students
were able to learn to help the people and perform any work as a team. A bus was hired for the

                                      Women’s Cell

The Women’s Cell was constituted in the College under the IQAC on the 6th September,
2013. The Cell constitutes of a Convenor, teacher members and students representatives.
The Women’s Cell was constituted for prevention/action against sexual and other forms of
harassment of women students of the college. The cell has a noble vision to generate a sense
of self respect and to equip women in the educational process with the capacity to become
leaders of the future, differentiating the right from the wrong while facing the challenges in
the society.




Guidelines and Functions
Enhancing self-esteem and self-confidence of women students, faculty and staff of the

college.

   •   To develop critical thinking ability of women students etc.
   •   To foster decision-making ability and action through collective processes.
   •   To enable women to make informed choices in areas like education, employment and
       health especially reproductive health.
   •   To enhance their participation on an equal footing in all areas.
   •   To inspire them for empowerment socially and financially through regular guidance
       & counseling.
   •   To make women students aware of the social responsibilities and give them mental
       support to fight against sexual and other forms of harassment of women students and
       for other women of the society through guidance and counseling.
   •   To encourage for undertaking minor research projects by small group of girl students.
   •   To take initiative for the establishment of Women’s Study Centre.

                                 COMPUTER & IT CELL
Under the aegis of IQAC (restructured in 2013), a new leaf has sprung up in the form of IT
Cell, which has opened up a gamut of avenues in the domain of technological support. A
language lab has been set up for advanced learners of the department of English. Usual chalk
and talk method is supplemented by audio visual aids. With the help of LCD, teachers are
able to take classes and seminar using PPTs and thus lead to interactive learning. Keeping in
view the importance of internet as a means for dissemination of information, the college
recently has taken the step of making the campus Wi-Fi enabled. Students are at liberty to
use high speed internet service within the confines of the college campus. The college has
one computer laboratory to cater to the needs of the students. The students are able to go
online and access information in the form of e-books and standard journals.

Composition of Computer & IT Cell:
       a) Sri Sudarshan Gupta, Assistant Professor, Deptt. of History              Convenor
       b) Dr. Rahul Chakraborty (Associate Prof. Deptt. of Bengali):               Member
       c) Smt. Sonali Choudhury (Librarian)                                        Member
       d) Sri Gouri Sankar Dhar, Junior Assistant                                  Member
       e) Kelhoukri Rutsa, Grade IV                                                Member

The use of technology and innovative ideas leads to best practices evolving in the library and
information environment. A number of computers have been installed in the college with
LAN connection and internet facilities in the Library, Computer Laboratory, Teachers’
Common Room, and Office etc. which helps in the creation and enhancement of
infrastructural facilities and technological up gradation necessary for improving the teaching-
learning process. The college also offers BSNL connection along with modem off campus to
the faculty. The Library has separate machines installed for internet browsing for students
and teachers offering institutional ID and Password for accessing e-resources over the
internet. Also information literacy training is given to the teachers and students to enlighten
them about library services, internet resources, e- resources and digital library which can
prove immensely helpful for them in teaching-learning and research activities. Besides,
networking is being established with other institutions like British Council Library,
INFLIBNET (NLIST) for online access of resources.


Again, use of ICT in imparting lessons is also encouraged. The IT Cell has taken the initiative
to orient the faculty in preparing power point presentations. Usual chalk and talk method is
supplemented by audio visual aids. With the help of LCD, teachers are able to take classes
and seminar using PPTs and thus lead to interactive learning. Smart board too is an important
tool for collaborative learning. The college has procured a smart board for interactive
teaching. From 2014, the college has started another innovative practice. Some of the
departments have prepared important topics in PPT mode and has handed over to the IT Cell.
The IT Cell then has uploaded the same in the college website. The idea is to incorporate
more topics subject wise in the coming years so as to make the website a repository of
learning.

The College has a separate Publication Cell under IQAC which have been publishing

“Research Journal of Radhamadhab College” has been accorded ISSN (ISSN 2250-3595).

The Cell follows a formulated publication policy. Articles are invited from scholars by means
of a notice which is circulated both in print and electronic format (in the college website)
along with the rules and regulations. After receiving the articles, the Editorial Board sends the
same for peer review. Eminent educationists are memvers of the peer review team. On the
basis of the peer review, the articles are either published or sent to the writer for changes, if
any, or are rejected. The Publication Cell excluding the Head Assistant comprises the
Editorial Board.

               CENTRE FOR EXTENSION EDUCATION
               FROM THE SESSION (2010-11 TO 2015-16)
Being an integral part of higher education in Southern Assam, Radhamadhab College, Silchar
established “Centre for Extension Education” on the day of 15th 2002, with the aims to
extend, spread and disseminate useful information and ideas to the rural people outside the
regularly organized educational system.

                                       MISSION
The mission of the Centre for Extension Education of Radhamadhab College, Silchar, is to
devote its energy and resources in the social development in the country by way of social
services, to make the community conscious of the scientific development and to develop a
scientific outlook in the various aspects of daily life of the people of the community.

       Objectives:
   •   To promote a sense of national integrity and communal harmony amongst citizens.
   •   To aware the members of the community about Population Explosion and the life
       killing diseases, and to encourage them to take preventive measures.
   •   To create awareness about increasing enviornmental hazards and to encourage for
       taking necessary measures for the protection of enviornment.
   •   To develop scientific temperament amongst the people of the community by
       educating them.
   •   To eradicate illiteracy by way of imparting education in the backward areas with
       special emphasis on female education.
   •   To help the Government and other Non-Government Organizations in the
       implementation of various socio-economic programmes at the grassroot level.

       Functions:
    • The Centre shall motivate students to participate in extension activities through
       organizing meetings, seminars, talks etc. in the college throughout the session.
    • The Centre shall decide the priority of the area of extension activities keeping in view
       the idea(s) as envisaged in the broad objective of the Centre.
    • The convenor is to make correspondences with various funding agencies for financial
       support of the Centre.

        of the Centre and shall resolve necessary measures accordingly.
     • Members of the Centre shall invite other interested faculty member to participate in
        the extension activities.
     • The Centre shall decide financial implications of the extension activities in different
        areas and shall recommend the same to the principal for release of financial grant for

     • The Centre shall maintain coordination with the IQAC and shall exchange views,

                  STUDENTS’ HEALTH CARE CENTRE


At a glance:

Introduction:-

Quality education cannot be imparted unless the students of the educational institution are
healthy and at the same time health conscious. Keeping this doctrine in view Students’ Health
Care Centre was established in Radhamadhab College in the year 2003. Since its inception,
the Health Care Centre is working relentlessly to provide health services to the students and
make them health conscious.

Aims and objectives of the Students’ Health Care Centre:

The Students’ Health Care Centre of Radhamadhab College is a provider of basic medical
facilities to the students of the college. The centre ensures periodical health check up by
medical practitioner. Health education being an integral part of the Health Centre, all possible
endeavour is made to arrange lectures on various health problems and information. The
centre also provides First-Aid services to the students. The centre takes initiative to arrange
health camps, publish newsletters and journals for making the students aware about health
education.

The centre particularly divides its nature of works in two categories. One is regular features
like health check up of the students and blood group diagnosing programme. In addition to
that, the centre organizes various other programmers like, workshop, guest lecture, etc in
every academic session to make the students health conscious. The centre also organizes
some health related programmes in collaboration with other NGOs and government
organizations.

KEY ACTIVITIES OF THE CENTRE

   •   Cancer awareness

   •   Blood Donation Camp

   •   Health Camp at different rural areas.



                                                                                            329
 From its inception the centre took the initiative to conduct various health related programmes
on different aspects, namely eye-check up programme, Dental camp, awareness programmme
on Swine Flu, AIDS, Cancer, Drug abuse, etc.

From academic session 2012-13, the centre took the initiative to extend its credibility in the
field of health especially for the interest of the community. Keeping this in view from the
session 2012-13, the centre conducted free health camp in every academic year in different
rural areas. This has been done considering the health problem of the poor and downtrodden
people of different remote parts of the district.

The centre already completed four free health camps at different rural areas. The first camp
was organized at Majhargram, second one at Bihara, 70 K. M. away from the town, third one
at Paloirbond Tea Estate and fourth one was at Rosekandi Tea Estate. These programmes are
generally conducted in collaboration with the local authorities.

The Students’ Health Care Centre under, IQAC is headed by an Executive Committee of
seven members along with a Convenor.

5. Arrangement:

As for the arrangement of the books in the library, they are classified according to ‘Dewey
Decimal Classification System’ (edition 20), which is a universal classification system
followed internationally. It is the method of application of Arabic numerals used decimally as
notation, to documents for bringing various materials from the same field together. Thus the
library books are arranged within each collection by their Subject Codes using Dewey
Decimal Classification (DDC) System. This system divides all knowledge as represented
by books and other materials, into nine main classes numbered by digits 1 to 9.
Materials too general to belong to any one of these classes, such as newspapers,
encyclopedias, bibliographies, etc fall into a tenth class numbered 0 which precedes the
others. Other main classes are written as hundreds. Therefore DDC codes for the main
subject groups are followed as:

       000-099    General Works
       100-199    Philosophy
       200-299    Religion
       300-399    Social Sciences
       400-499    Language
       500-599    Natural Sciences
       600-699    Applied Sciences
       700-799    Arts
       800-899    Literature
       900-999    History & Geography


These are further subdivided into nine sections again from 1-9 based on the subdivisions of
the subject. Further divisions may also be made, as may be necessary by the addition of
more digits following a decimal point after three digits. The number so derived is called the
‘Class No.’ of the book. A ‘Book No.’ is also assigned to the book which defines the author
of the book, using the first three letters of the author’s surname. For example, a book on
‘History of English Literature’ by David Daiches would be classified as 820.09(Class


                                                                                           348
 No.)/DAI (Book No.).This together is called the ‘Call No.’ of the book, which is the most
important entity for arranging the books in the library in a systematic order.
For Cataloguing of the books, the library maintains the Anglo-American Cataloguing
Rules,2nd ed.(AACRII), in which the entries of the books are arranged author-wise, giving
details like title, author, edition, publication, series, ISBN, etc. and arranged alphabetically
within each subject, in the catalogue cabinet. This gives complete bibliographical information
of the library collection. In subsequent time this manual system of Catalogue has been
discontinued with the advent of modern and sophisticated system of catalogue-OPAC in the
library.




6.     Cataloguing: OPAC:

An OPAC (Online Public Access Catalogue) is an online database/catalogue of resources
available in the library which principally helps to search a book in the library with the help of
a computer. Users search a library catalog primarily to locate books and other material
physically located at a library. OPAC provides online searching and easy retrieval of books
along with their location, through the following access points on the computer screen:

           •   By title/keywords in title
           •   By author
           •   By co-author
           •   By editor
           •   By subject
           •   By Call No.
           •   By Section / Category

It may be mentioned here that the OPAC Module of the Library Database has also been
uploaded in the library page of the college website, so that the collection of the library may
be browsed sitting at home, through the internet. This system of OPAC is chiefly known as

       •   Awareness of library services
       •   Relevance/pertinence of results
       •   Ease of access
       •   Quality of reference service
       •   Effectiveness of outreach efforts
       •   Responsiveness to requests
       •   What services are being utilized
       •   Unmet needs
       •   Why services are not being used
       •   Training needs
       •   What documents/document types are most important
       •   What access tools are most important
The feedback so obtained is analyzed to find out the limitation if any regarding services and
facilities of the library and also the plausible suggestions from the users, which may be
incorporated in the library management system. Besides this, the student user groups are
verbally interrogated to know their problems and their needs. Also they are given the scope to
recommend important text books for their course, which they want to have in the library for
their class and examination purpose. The periodic meetings of the Library Advisory
Committee also enlightens with constructive suggestions.

15.      Infrastructure:

Library is having a Digital Library Server, which host educational CDs, DVDs, downloaded
e-books and other digital resources. Besides this, it has a Library Database in the main server
of the library bearing the full record of the library collection and library members. There are
eight computers in the Digital Section library to facilitate information accessing by users.
Seperate computers have been assigned for Internet browsing and OPAC terminals (online
searching) specifically for students and faculty, in which they can also access the Library is
having Xerox machine, TV, Scanner, HP LaserJet Printer, 10 no. of PCs, Multimedia

                                                                                           358
 Projector, Online and offline UPS, stabilizer, etc. Library is using SOUL 2.0 integrated
library management software for automating various functions in the Library like book
acquisition, circulation, cataloguing and serial control. Library is using Bar Code technology
in Circulation tasks and other automated jobs of the library.

As regards the IT infrastructure, the library has built a Local Area Network (LAN) around
UTP CAT5 Cable with routing switches and has an Internet bandwidth of 1Gbps. The library
has 02 servers, 10 PCs and other accessories adequate to cater to the needs of users for
accessing Internet, OPAC, Digital Library, E-books, E-journals and other E-resources. The
reading area in the library has been Wi-Fi enabled to provide wireless access to the Internet.
Users are welcome to use their laptops in the library.

15. SWOC Analysis:


Following is an analysis of the library’s strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and challenges
it faces in the current environment. Some identified items have a direct relationship to the
development of the library while others apply in a more general way:
   i) Strength:
               • Qualified Staff who has degree/diploma in Library and Information Sc.
               • Different types of collection
                Free Internet access and Wi-Fi
                Library Webpage giving links to e-resources
                User Orientation Programmes
                Introduction of IT oriented facilities
                Library Automation
                Electronic resources and initiation of Digital Library
                Healthy Acquisition Policy involving all the academic departments,
               organizing Book Exhibitions, etc.
                Special collection on Barak Valley to preserve the literary and cultural
               heritage of the region
   ii) Weakness:
           •    Lack of space
           •    Rural target group

                                                                                               359
        •   Lack of awareness about computer and IT among users
       •   Shortage of staff
       •   Constraints of funds
iii) Opportunities:
       •   Library can support the teaching-learning process of the college to a great
           extent.
       •   Library can prove immensely helpful to the students to help them in their
           career preparations, academics, curricular activities, etc.
       • Readers can use the library in an effective manner to access the reading
           materials within and outside the library walls through Internet.
       • The e-resources of the library can help the teachers in their research activities.
       • Readers can avail the scanning, printing and downloading facilities of the
           library to get their document of choice.
iv) Challenges:
       •   The Digital Library is still on the process of improvisation and needs to be
           strengthened further with more digital items.
       •   More orientations and instruction programmes are required to create
           awareness amongst the library users in order to ensure optimal use of the
           library, especially the electronic resources.
       •   More computers are required for the benefit of the users.
       •   A separate Library building with a spacious Reading Room is important to
           give a congenial reading atmosphere.


16. Future Plans:

The library plans to have a separate library building of its own and also to make provision
for   spacious Reading Rooms for the benefit of the faculty and especially the students.
The library plans to make better arrangements for designing the separate sections and
collections of the library. The library shall also put an effort to strengthen the IT
infrastructure of the library and stress on the e-resource development in the library.
